clue.text: A pipe for the judge

explanation.surface: A tobacco pipe being handed to a judge in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A recorder is a wooden end-blown flute, a kind of pipe, and in England a Recorder is also a part-time criminal judge.

clue.text: See about a drink for a journalist

parts.note: re, as in a letter's 'see about' or 'concerning'
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: Arranging a round of drinks for a newspaper hack.
explanation.definitionFit: A reporter is a journalist who gathers and writes news.

clue.text: They advertise a deity under the Big Top

indicators.note: under the tent means this god is placed inside the circus word

parts.note: the big top is a circus tent, standing for the circus
a lar is a Roman household god, one of the Lares

explanation.surface: Posters promote a god appearing in the circus ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under the Big Top' looks like a circus act; the Big Top stands for the circus itself, and 'under' sets the god inside it. Lares were Roman household gods.
explanation.definitionFit: Circulars are printed notices sent out widely to promote goods.

clue.text: Groovy kind of bird, likely to go off!

definitions.text: Groovy kind of bird, likely to go off!

parts.words: Groovy kind of bird, likely to go off!
parts.note: a weapon with a spirally grooved barrel, which also names an Australian bird of paradise and is liable to fire

explanation.surface: A trendy bird that is about to explode with excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groovy' looks like slang for fashionable; it means having grooves cut in the barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle's barrel is grooved, the riflebird is a bird of paradise, and a loaded gun may go off.

clue.text: Pastoral idyll

parts.note: a short poem of country life such as Virgil wrote

explanation.definitionFit: An eclogue is a short pastoral poem, a dialogue between shepherds.

clue.text: A soft chime has charm

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for soft
a peal is a ringing of bells, a chime

explanation.surface: A gentle ring of bells is charming.
explanation.definitionFit: Appeal is attractiveness, the same quality as charm.

clue.text: It's a way they have in the transport world

definitions.text: It's a way they have in the transport world

parts.words: It's a way they have in the transport world
parts.note: railwaymen call the finished track of a line by a phrase ending in way

explanation.surface: A habit peculiar to people who work in transport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a way they have' reads as a habit; it is the permanent way, British railway jargon for the track and its bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The permanent way is railway track, so the first word with 'way' names the transport term.

clue.text: Lady recipient of John's second epistle

definitions.text: Lady recipient of John's second epistle

parts.words: Lady recipient of John's second epistle
parts.note: the Second Letter of John in the New Testament opens by addressing a chosen woman

explanation.surface: The woman to whom St John wrote his second letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 John begins 'The elder unto the elect lady', in the Authorised Version.
explanation.definitionFit: Elect means chosen, the word that describes the lady to whom the epistle is written.

clue.text: Kipling's lady holds an article in one dimension

indicators.note: holds means the ship's word contains the article

parts.note: Kipling wrote 'The Liner She's a Lady', so a liner is his lady
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A woman in Kipling's verse contains a piece of writing about a single dimension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' puts A inside LINER, before the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Linear means extending along a line, in one dimension only.

clue.text: Rangers' ground has a big enclosure

explanation.surface: Rangers football club's stadium has a large stand.
explanation.walkthrough: Rangers looks like the Glasgow football club; they are cowboys on the range.
explanation.definitionFit: A corral is a pen where ranchers keep cattle or horses, a large enclosure.

clue.text: A case for the Minister ?

parts.note: a government minister carries papers in a flat case, and the same word names the ministerial office itself

explanation.surface: A matter to be referred to a government minister.
explanation.walkthrough: The case is both the leather document case and the department a minister holds; a minister 'without' one has no department.
explanation.definitionFit: A portfolio is a flat case for papers and also the office held by a minister.

clue.text: German river sounds clean!

indicators.note: sounds says the word for clean is heard rather than spelt out here

parts.note: to rinse is to clean with water

explanation.surface: A German waterway noted for sounding pure.
explanation.walkthrough: The German spelling of the Rhine, said with its possessive (the river's), is close in sound to the verb rinse.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhein is the German name of the Rhine, a major river of Germany.

clue.text: Dragon who might make one blush!

explanation.surface: A fearsome beast whose remarks cause embarrassment.
explanation.definitionFit: Rouge Dragon is a herald of the College of Arms in London; rouge is also red make-up that gives the cheeks a blushing colour.

clue.text: Aunt R. gaga ? What's the big idea ?

indicators.note: the question mark here asks the solver to rearrange the senile aunt's letters

explanation.surface: Someone's aunt has gone senile and is asking what is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no anagram word: the question mark alone signals that AUNTRGAGA is to be rearranged. 'What's the big idea?' puns on Rabelais's giant.
explanation.definitionFit: Gargantua is the giant of Rabelais, so his name stands for the idea of hugeness.

clue.text: Philippe the revolutionary

parts.note: the Duke of Orleans who sided with the French Revolution took a slogan word as his surname

explanation.surface: A French radical named Philippe.
explanation.walkthrough: Louis Philippe, Duke of Orleans, renamed himself Philippe Egalite (equality) to show his support for the Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: Equality, one of the three words of the French revolutionary motto, was the name the revolutionary duke adopted.

clue.text: Cockney quality in a Landseer dog

explanation.surface: A dog in a Victorian painting has the cheek of a Londoner.
explanation.walkthrough: Landseer painted 'Dignity and Impudence', two dogs; Cockneys, East Londoners, are known for their cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: Impudence is cheek, a trait credited to Cockneys, and is the name of the small terrier in Landseer's picture.

clue.text: Has to be made up like a Confederate general

explanation.surface: Something must be invented, in the manner of General Lee.
explanation.walkthrough: Ships drifting to leeward must make up the lost distance; read in two words it is the way of Lee, the Confederate commander.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is lost ground that must be recovered, and split as Lee way it means in the manner of Robert E. Lee.

clue.text: Bitter-sweet when a Spanish hero falls

parts.note: El Cid was the medieval Castilian warrior hero
drops means falls

explanation.surface: A sad moment when a Spanish champion is defeated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bitter-sweet' is a description of the sour boiled sweets, not of a mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid drops are sharp-tasting boiled sweets, sour yet sugary.

clue.text: Early bat that gives the game away

definitions.text: Early bat that gives the game away

indicators.note: giving the game away here means these two words surrender their letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricketer's early swing reveals the plan.
explanation.walkthrough: As an &lit, the whole clue defines the answer, and 'gives the game away' also tells you to rearrange EARLYBAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A betrayal reveals a secret, as giving the game away does.

clue.text: Path is deflected to the dump

indicators.note: deflected means the letters of these words are sent off course into a new order

explanation.surface: A footpath has been diverted towards the rubbish tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deflected' rearranges PATHIS.
explanation.definitionFit: An ash-pit is where ashes and refuse are dumped, a small rubbish dump.

clue.text: Manages free drinks

explanation.surface: Someone runs the bar and hands out complimentary drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat a matter is to deal with it, and treats are things paid for on another's behalf, like a round.

clue.text: Rope for well-drilled deserters ?

explanation.surface: A rope intended for a disciplined band of runaways.
explanation.walkthrough: Rats desert a sinking ship, so well-drilled rats stand in a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratline is one of the small ropes forming the rungs of a ship's shrouds; read as two words it is a row of disciplined rats.

clue.text: . the fatal egg by pleasure laid " (Cowper)

definitions.text: the fatal egg by pleasure laid

parts.words: the fatal egg by pleasure laid
parts.note: a line from William Cowper naming the guilt that self-indulgence hatches

explanation.surface: A quotation from an eighteenth-century poet with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank is filled from Cowper's 'The Progress of Error': the missing word opens the line.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowper calls the guilt bred by indulgence a fatal egg laid by pleasure.

clue.text: Scintillating type, the wireless operator

explanation.surface: A dazzling person who runs the radio room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sparks' is the old nickname for a ship's radio operator.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who throws off flashes of wit, and the nickname of the radio man aboard ship.

clue.text: Fancy, it goes up in smoke

explanation.surface: An imaginative notion that vanishes into thin air.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is said to come from opium-pipe visions, so it literally goes up in smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe dream is a fanciful hope, and a pipe's contents are burnt to smoke.

clue.text: Entails work for the extremely pushful

definitions.text: Entails work for the extremely pushful

parts.words: Entails work for the extremely pushful
parts.note: a lever worked by the feet, which demands effort from whoever pushes on it

explanation.surface: Pushy people have to put in hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pushful' looks like ambitious; it means pressing down with the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedal is a foot lever that must be pushed to drive a bicycle.

clue.text: One who sounds partial to drink ?

indicators.note: sounds says we hear the word for a partisan, not see it

parts.note: someone partial takes sides, so is a sider

explanation.surface: A person who seems to be fond of alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One who ... partial' is a sider, one who takes sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Cider is an alcoholic drink made from fermented apples.

clue.text: Civic mourner ?

parts.note: a town official who calls out news, read as one who weeps

explanation.surface: A council official who grieves.
explanation.walkthrough: The town official calls out proclamations; the question mark lets 'mourner' read as one who cries.
explanation.definitionFit: A town crier shouts public announcements, and anyone who weeps cries.

clue.text: His kiss was stony !

parts.note: the kiss here is a famous marble sculpture of two lovers, so it is made of stone

explanation.surface: A man whose kisses were cold and unfeeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stony' suggests a cold lover; it means carved in marble.
explanation.definitionFit: The French sculptor carved The Kiss in marble.

clue.text: Land wanted !

parts.note: read as a demand for ground, as by an expanding power claiming more domain

explanation.surface: A cry for ground to be ceded.
explanation.definitionFit: Territory is land under a ruler's control, the thing a conquering nation demands.

clue.text: It's all in the set of the helmet

indicators.note: in means one word is placed inside the other

explanation.surface: Everything depends on how a helmet sits on the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's all in the set' reads as a remark about how the helmet sits; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sallet is a light medieval helmet with a flared back.

clue.text: Tit for tat

parts.note: the idiom for paying back like with like, as an act of retaliation

explanation.definitionFit: Tit for tat means retaliation in kind, an act of revenge.
